chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu

Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man who had some dinars with me, and he was ill. So he said to me, 'If something happens to me, give so-and-so twenty dinars, and give my brother the remainder of the dinars.' So he died, and I did not witness his death. Then a truthful Muslim man came to me and said to me, 'He ordered me to say to you: Look at the dinars which I ordered you to give to my brother, so give in charity from them ten dinars, distribute them among the Muslims.' And his brother did not know that he had anything with me. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I view that you should give in charity from them ten dinars, just as he said.'
ai.seo_question: How to handle a modification in a will regarding inheritance and charity after death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of revocability in bequests (*wasiyya*) prior to death, where the final communicated instruction supersedes the initial one, even if it alters the beneficiary's share. Scholarly commentary highlights that the brother's lack of prior knowledge does not invalidate the change, emphasizing the testator's autonomy over their estate until the moment of death. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic inheritance law regarding charitable deductions from specific bequests.
